mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) relative to its historical average indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance, which reduces the cost of capital and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 4.0% (25th percentile of 5-year history), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% (a threshold indicating monetary tightening) compresses equity valuations by raising the discount rate, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a deteriorating labor market, which signals potential economic slowdown and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances where UNRATE rises >0.2pp and PAYEMS falls >50k in the same month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, strong housing starts (HOUST) and robust retail sales (RSAFS) above their 5-year averages signal that the economic cycle is nearing its peak, prompting profit-taking and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when the regime is late-cycle expansion and HOUST > 105 and RSAFS > 350000, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) relative to its historical average indicates robust manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when INDPRO > 110 (5-year average), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 5.0% (a threshold indicating labor market stress) signals potential economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and decline in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a potential shift in consumer spending patterns, which may signal economic imbalances and lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances where HOUST rises >0.5% and RSAFS falls >0.3% in the same month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%), a rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals an increased likelihood of aggressive monetary tightening, which compresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.5% and CPIAUCSL rises >0.2%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is <0.03.
